lessons.title: Unit 0: Learn How to Read Hangul
lessons.explanation: Learn the Korean alphabet, syllable blocks, consonants, vowels and the combinations needed to read Korean words.
lessons.meaning: HTSK Unit 0 teaches basic Korean consonants and vowels, syllable blocks, final consonants, additional letters and combined vowels. It also recommends moving away from romanization and using Korean audio and reading practice.
lessons.when_to_use: Use this unit before grammar to learn to read and pronounce Korean syllable blocks without relying on romanization.
lessons.how_to_build: Build one syllable block from a consonant and vowel; add a final consonant underneath when needed. Continue with the additional letters and combined vowels in the next Unit 0 lessons.
examples: Combine two vowels into a complex vowel.
Combine ㄴ and ㅏ into one syllable.
lessons.examples_source: How to Study Korean lesson-based sentence practice

lessons.title: Basic sentence structure and 이다
lessons.explanation: Learn the basic structure of Korean sentences and how to make sentences with 이다 (“to be”).
lessons.meaning: Learn the basic structure of Korean sentences and how to make sentences with 이다 (“to be”).
lessons.when_to_use: Use 이다 to identify people and things: “A is B.” It is the basic Korean noun-predicate pattern.
lessons.how_to_build: Attach 이에요 after a noun ending in a consonant and 예요 after a noun ending in a vowel. The noun before 이다 is the thing being identified.

lessons.title: 이/가 and 있다
lessons.explanation: Learn the subject particles 이/가 and use 있다 to express existence, location and possession.
lessons.meaning: Learn the subject particles 이/가 and use 있다 to express existence, location and possession.
lessons.when_to_use: Use 이/가 to mark the subject and 있다 for existence, location and possession.
lessons.how_to_build: Attach 이 after a consonant and 가 after a vowel. 있다 can mean “exist/be located” or “have,” depending on the sentence.

My younger sibling is at school.

lessons.meaning: Learn to make sentences with adjectives and verbs, express possession with 의, and distinguish 좋다 from 좋아하다.

lessons.title: 적 and 스럽다
lessons.explanation: Learn how 적 and 스럽다 attach to words and change their meaning.
lessons.meaning: Learn how 적 and 스럽다 attach to words and change their meaning.
lessons.when_to_use: Use 적 and 스럽다 to derive related adjectives and describe qualities such as “cultural” or “natural.”
lessons.how_to_build: Attach 적 to certain nouns to make “-al/-ic” adjectives and 스럽다 to express a quality or characteristic; apply normal adjective conjugation afterward.
lessons.examples_source: How to Study Korean lesson-based sentence practice

lessons.title: Connecting clauses with 고
lessons.explanation: Use 고 to connect ideas and use 고 싶다 to express a desire to do something.
lessons.meaning: Use 고 to connect ideas and use 고 싶다 to express a desire to do something.
lessons.when_to_use: Use 고 to connect clauses and 고 싶다 to say that you want to do something.
lessons.how_to_build: Attach 고 to the first clause and conjugate the final clause. For desire, attach 고 싶다 to the verb stem.
examples: I want to go to Korea.
I read a book and listened to music.
I ate breakfast and went to school.
lessons.examples_source: How to Study Korean lesson-based sentence practice

lessons.title: Progressive and change of state
lessons.explanation: Use 고 있다 for an ongoing action and 아/어지다 to express becoming a certain way.
lessons.meaning: Use 고 있다 for an ongoing action and 아/어지다 to express becoming a certain way.
lessons.when_to_use: Use 고 있다 for an action in progress and 아/어지다 when a quality or state changes.
lessons.how_to_build: Attach 고 있다 to the verb stem for an ongoing action; attach 아/어지다 to an adjective stem for “become/get.”
examples: I am reading a book now.
I am waiting for my friend.

lessons.title: Comparatives and superlatives
lessons.explanation: Make comparative and superlative sentences and understand the common word 더.
lessons.meaning: Make comparative and superlative sentences and understand the common word 더.
lessons.when_to_use: Use 보다 for “more ... than” and 제일/가장 for “the most”; 더 means “more.”
lessons.how_to_build: Put 보다 after the comparison target and 더 before the comparative adjective; put 제일 or 가장 before the superlative expression.
examples: Korean is more difficult than English.
This bag is more expensive than that bag.
Seoul is the biggest in Korea.

lessons.title: 잘 and 못
lessons.explanation: Learn how 잘 and 못 express doing something well or poorly and how they differ from 잘하다 and 못하다.
lessons.meaning: Learn how 잘 and 못 express doing something well or poorly and how they differ from 잘하다 and 못하다.
lessons.when_to_use: Use 잘 and 못 before a verb for doing something well or poorly, and 잘하다/못하다 when the whole ability is the predicate.
lessons.how_to_build: Put 잘 or 못 before the verb for manner/ability; use 잘하다 or 못하다 as lexical predicates meaning to be good or bad at an activity.

lessons.title: Questions I
lessons.explanation: Form questions without question words and use common words such as who, what, when, why and where.
lessons.meaning: Form questions without question words and use common words such as who, what, when, why and where.
lessons.when_to_use: Use Korean question intonation and question words such as 누구, 뭐, 언제, 왜 and 어디.
lessons.how_to_build: Keep the question word in the position of the missing information: 누구 for a person, 뭐 for a thing, 언제 for time, 왜 for reason and 어디 for place.
examples: When did you go to school?
lessons.examples_source: How to Study Korean lesson-based sentence practice

lessons.title: ㅎ irregular and colors
lessons.explanation: Use the ㅎ irregular with colors and with 이렇다, 그렇다 and 저렇다.
lessons.meaning: Use the ㅎ irregular with colors and with 이렇다, 그렇다 and 저렇다.
lessons.when_to_use: Use the ㅎ irregular with relevant adjectives such as colors and with 이렇다, 그렇다 and 저렇다.
lessons.how_to_build: When a ㅎ-irregular adjective meets a vowel beginning ending, ㅎ disappears and the vowel changes according to the irregular pattern.
examples: What kind of color is it?
What kind of person is he/she?
What kind of shape is it?

lessons.title: Time expressions and indefinite words
lessons.explanation: Use time words meaning before, after, since and within, and learn indefinite expressions.
lessons.meaning: Use time words meaning before, after, since and within, and learn indefinite expressions.
lessons.when_to_use: Use 전, 후, 이래로 and 이내 to position events in time, and indefinite words to mean anybody, somebody or everybody.
lessons.how_to_build: Place 전/후/이래로/이내 after the relevant time expression; combine 누구/뭐/어디 with -든지 or related forms for indefinite meanings.
examples: I will finish within one month.
lessons.examples_source: How to Study Korean lesson-based sentence practice
